title: AI-Anxiety, Hope, and Techno-Subjunctivity: Expanding Psychoanalytic Identity for the AI Age
abstract: This article recognizes that the artificial intelligence (AI) age is reconfiguring conditions for intimacy, clinical care, and psychoanalytic professional identity. Beginning with AI-anxiety as a response to transformative change and technological peril, it highlights hope, not as optimism but as an active way of being that permits sustained engagement. Against the reassuring claim that machines can never do what psychoanalysts do, the article distinguishes performance from process: Relational AI may soon replicate expert clinical behavior without replicating human subjectivity, embodiment, or unconscious life. What remains irreducible is the meaning-making context of human care, including the fact that analytic speech acts derive meaning and force from being offered by a vulnerable, invested human other. The article then introduces techno-subjunctivity to describe the new relational field created by anthropomorphic AI: an illusion of intimacy in which users oscillate between feeling recognized by a responsive other while knowing they are interacting with a machine without interiority. Psychoanalytic identity, the article concludes, must expand to include AI-fitness. Such direct experience with AI’s relational pull along with critical psychoanalytic reflection will enable clinicians to accompany patients and students through techno-subjunctive life without denial, shame, or surrender.

journal.name: JOURNAL OF THE AMERICAN PSYCHOANALYTIC ASSOCIATION
